generations.name: First generation (24 kWh)
generations.notes: Launch (ZE0/AZE0): 24 kWh pack, optional CHAdeMO (~50 kW). Split at 2016 because the 30 kWh pack arrived then. The CHAdeMO peak (~50 kW) is general knowledge, not from a fetched page. Canada first sold the Leaf for MY2012 (general knowledge, not verified here). Confidence: medium (researched 2026-11-19, owner review pending). Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nissan_Leaf ; https://usa.nissannews.com/en-US/releases/release-9c04406501da47ec83c0c3138bf6a5f5-nissan-announces-u-s-pricing-for-2016-leaf

generations.name: First generation (30 kWh)
generations.notes: 30 kWh pack, same footprint, on SV/SL for 2016 and all trims for 2017 (2016 S kept 24 kWh). This is a mid-generation pack change, not a new generation; it could also be modelled as a variant within one first generation. The 2017 all-trims 30 kWh claim comes from secondary sources. Confidence: medium (researched 2026-11-19, owner review pending). Sources: https://usa.nissannews.com/en-US/releases/release-9c04406501da47ec83c0c3138bf6a5f5-nissan-announces-u-s-pricing-for-2016-leaf ; https://insideevs.com/news/326562/2016-nissan-leaf-107-miles-epa-range-full-specs-pricing/

generations.name: Second generation (ZE1)
generations.notes: All-new body: 40 kWh pack (CHAdeMO ~50 kW); 62 kWh Leaf Plus from 2019 (CHAdeMO up to ~100 kW). The 62 kWh Plus (2019+) is a variant addition, not a line-wide change, so not split. Canada had no S trim for 2025. Same model years in CA and US. Confidence: high (researched 2026-11-19, owner review pending). Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nissan_Leaf ; https://www.cars.com/articles/2025-nissan-leaf-unchanged-loses-ev-tax-credit-485068/ ; https://rpmweb.ca/actualites-et-chroniques/actualites/nouvelles/la-nissan-leaf-sera-toujours-offerte-en-2025-dans-la-meme-configuration

generations.name: Third generation (ZE2)
generations.notes: All-new crossover on CMF-EV: 52 kWh and 75 kWh liquid-cooled NMC packs; native NACS port (replaces CHAdeMO); DC up to 150 kW. Canada launched with the 75 kWh pack first; the small pack is reported as 52 or 53 kWh depending on source. Confidence: high (researched 2026-11-19, owner review pending). Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nissan_Leaf ; https://driveteslacanada.ca/news/2026-nissan-leaf-debuts-with-up-to-488-km-range-new-styling-and-nacs-charging/ ; https://electricautonomy.ca/automakers/passenger-electric-vehicles/2025-07-17/2026-nissan-leaf-canada-availability/
